blocks.text: Langley City map, zoning map and postal code

Langley City (the City of Langley) and Langley Township are separate municipalities, each with its own zoning bylaw and zoning map. In the City, Zoning Bylaw No. 3300 (2025) applies. The City’s Interactive Map lets you search an address and see properties, streets, parks, utilities and air photos, and the City posts free PDF maps, including a Langley City Map and a Map of the Langleys showing the City and the Township.

Downtown Langley postal codes start with V3A. A postal code does not settle whether a home is in the City or the Township; the property tax notice does, and so does the address search on the City’s Interactive Map.

items.t: On MLS®: the Langley City sub-area is one of 11 sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Langley" (Aldergrove, Brookswood, Campbell Valley, County Line Glen Valley, Fort Langley, Langley City, Murrayville, Otter District, Salmon River, Walnut Grove, Willoughby Heights).

Where the condos are: the apartment buildings I know of in the City are one older group, three buildings from 1988–1990 within a few blocks of each other around 205 Street, 206 Street and 53 Avenue downtown.

Langley City sub-area, September 2026 — the area's own figures (inventory / sales / sales ratio): Detached 64 / 8 / 13%; Condos & Townhomes 195 / 34 / 17% (joint with Aldergrove in the Langley set, below Murrayville 23%, Willoughby Heights 19% and Walnut Grove 18%). SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, and the only community here is the combined City + Township "Langley".

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Langley City

items.t: Secondary suites (City Zoning Bylaw No. 3300): a suite can be no larger than 100 m² or 40% of the building's floor area, whichever is smaller. The owner must live on the property, there must be at least one extra parking space, and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and listed in the City's suite registry.

Langley City property taxes: payments received after the July 2 due date incur a penalty; the City's payment page lists City Hall at 20399 Douglas Crescent and a 2.2% processing fee on credit-card payments.

blocks.text: Good to know about Langley City condos

items.t: Parkway Estates (1988), Parkway II (1989) and Glenmont Park (1990) stand within a few blocks of each other around 205 Street, 206 Street and 53 Avenue, and all three are published as 55+ communities — a City condo search is, in practice, a search of those three buildings and their strata documents, whatever the 252-result feed suggests.

Two addresses ten numbers apart are different buildings with different records. Glenmont Park is 5375 205 St; Morningside Estates is 5365 205 St. Directory and listing searches blur the pair — verify the civic address on the Form B before importing any fact from one to the other.

The Langleys' hospital is not in the City. Langley Memorial Hospital's Fraser Health listing places it at 22051 Fraser Highway, in the Township of Langley, immediately outside the City boundary, though it is the hospital City residents use.

Langley City has no station today; the City's own vision page states SkyTrain is coming "by the end of 2029" — pricing a City condo on a station that does not yet exist is pricing the City's published anticipation, not current service.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Langley City

items.t: Zoning: City of Langley Zoning Bylaw, 2025, No. 3300, which repeals Zoning Bylaw 1996 No. 2100.
City property taxes: payments received after the July 2 due date incur a penalty; the City's payment page lists City Hall at 20399 Douglas Crescent and a 2.2% processing fee on credit-card payments.

In the Township of Langley (not the City): small-scale multi-unit housing is under Bylaw 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024); suites are capped at 120 m²; and a coach house is a fee-simple second unit, never strata. Sources disagree on suites in townhouses: the zoning bylaw allows them at 120 m², but the Township's January 2025 guide says they aren't permitted, so check with the Township. The Willoughby Community Plan (Bylaw 1836, 1979) is now Schedule 6 of Bylaw 6200 (adopted December 1, 2025); the Willoughby plan update bylaws had only first and second reading on May 25, 2026.

Local rules that affect land buyers in Langley City

items.t: Zoning in the City of Langley: City Zoning Bylaw No. 3300 (2025) applies, replacing Bylaw No. 2100. Minimum lot sizes: R1 Suburban Residential 557 m² with 16 m of frontage; R2 Townhouse Residential 1,000 m² (except party-wall lots created by subdivision: up to 280 m², 4.5 m frontage); R3 Low Rise Residential 1,000 m² with 26 m of frontage. The Township's Bylaw 2500 doesn't apply in the City.

Small-scale multi-unit housing in the City: the City changed its Zoning Bylaw to allow small-scale multi-unit housing on RS1 and RS2 lots (Bylaw No. 3284). These are the City's own rules; the Township's are different.

Suites in the City: a secondary suite can be no larger than 100 m² or 40% of the main home's floor area, whichever is smaller. The owner must live on the property, there must be at least one extra parking space, and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and listed in the City's suite registry.

Subdividing in the City: under Bylaw 3300, land can only be subdivided as the bylaw allows. Subdivisions are also subject to the City's Subdivision Control Bylaw and Development Cost Charge Bylaw (No. 3256, 2024), and new lots must meet their zone's minimum lot size. Meeting the minimums doesn't guarantee the City's Approving Officer will approve it.

Strata rules (for any bare-land strata lot): the Form B must be provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page. Since July 1, 2024, stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and since November 1, 2023 at least 10% of the budget must go into the contingency reserve. Rental restriction bylaws have been void since November 24, 2022, and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older (with exemptions from May 1, 2023). None of this applies to a fee-simple lot.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Langley City
Local rules that affect duplexes in Langley City

items.t: Small-scale housing and suites in Langley City: Bylaw No. 3284 (adopted June 17, 2024) allows 4 units on RS1 and RS2 lots, or 6 within 400 m of a frequent bus stop. Under Zoning Bylaw No. 3300, a secondary suite can be no larger than 100 m² or 40% of the building's floor area, whichever is smaller. The owner must live on the property, there must be at least one extra parking space, and the suite must be inspected, approved through a building permit and listed in the City's suite registry. The same cap applies to a suite in a City duplex as in a single-family house.
